Slowing her descent with her knife puncturing the lung of the wolf she’d struck the side of, Kara dropped fifteen feet to the ground, jarring her knees, and dashed forward at the sight of one wolf advancing on Lena’s unconscious form.

     

                Grabbing its tail, she jerked it back with all her might, not enough to draw it away but enough to stop it in its tracks. Sweating and breathing heavily, Kara knotted her sword hand in the matted fur and then hefter her long knife, giving the blade a quick kiss before she sent it hilt-over-tip towards the turning head, catching the wolf in the throat. She felt claws rake her back, blunted somewhat by the layers of her cloak and clothes as the wolf pinned her face-down, the size of its paw bigger than Kara’s whole back as she gritted her teeth and struggled beneath the weight of it.

     

                She was still struggling when an arrow cut through the air and punched through the eye of one of the wolves as it yelped and buckled, its paws gouging deep furrows in the soft mud along the stream as it tried to rise again and faltered. Staggering to her feet and lurching towards her wife, Kara whirled around, knees bent as she defensively hunched over Lena, trying to catch sight of the newcomer and whether they were a threat to Kara, who knew she was back on Seelie ground but had been hunted the whole way. A ripple of shock crossed her face as she caught sight of a figure in black leathers fitting another arrow to her bow and letting it loose at another wolf. This one struck the meaty part of the creature’s thigh, the fleshy fronds of a sprouting mushroom split by the trajectory of the arrow as the wolf snarled, limping as it tried to circle Reign.

     

                Two of them were circling, hackles raised, while the other three spouted putrefied black blood, dead or in the process of dying, and Kara had a split second to take in the sight of Reign and Andrea, who was lingering back, before she deemed the wolves a bigger threat. Fire blossomed in the palms of Andrea’s hands and Kara was accustomed to wielding water near flame, thanks to her many forays into battle with Alex, so she summoned a whip of water and set it to steam above the heat of the fire, obscuring them for a moment as Reign skulked forward and sprung up onto the shoulder of one and used the momentum to launch herself onto the other’s back. 

     

                Kara got a whiff of singing fur as Reign buried her own flame-wreathed hand into the scruff of its neck, and wielding her water, Kara beat back the other wolf as she let the hunter and attendant take care of the other. She was tired though, so very tired and bleeding freely from her wounds, every muscle and bone aching and bruised, so it was all she could do to fend off the wolf as she stayed near Lena, until Reign and Andrea had filled the valley with acrid smoke and sizzling flesh before they turned on the last wolf as one. As soon as the last wolf dropped dead with three of Reign’s throwing knives in its neck and the smell of burning pelt and flesh from Andrea’s flames, Kara pivoted and had her sword pressed against the neck of the hunter.

     

                “What are you doing here?” Kara demanded, her anger brittle and exhausted after the ordeal of her day. 

     

                “Your gratitude is lacking.”

     

                “I won’t ask again.”

     

                Rolling her eyes, Andrea stepped forward and jerked Reign back by the neck of her leather jerkin. “Use your sword against your enemies, you witless Seelie. We are not them.”

     

                Narrowing her blue eyes a fraction, Kara’s mouth twisted derisively at the words spoken in the fae language. Bindingly honest but, nevertheless, sceptically accepted. “You may speak truthfully but am I to believe the Queen’s hound has tracked us out of the goodness of her shrivelled heart? A dog is loyal to its master.”

     

                “Perhaps I’ve escaped my collar,” Reign said with amusement.

     

                “We may discuss the mistrust between the four of us once camp has been made,” Andrea grumpily proclaimed, drawing her cloak tighter around herself as she looked up at the darkening sky. “Night isn’t far and I don’t know this Court well enough to be sure how far the nearest safe holdings are.”

     

                “The nearest safe holding is hours away yet. We won’t reach it before nightfall,” Kara muttered, sinking to a crouch to uproot a fistful of moss and wipe both of her blades clean. “Our horses have fled and she’s in no state to travel. We shall have to camp here; there will be safety in numbers, at the very least.”

     

                Kara gestured dismissively at Lena, who was out cold, her face a shocking shade of alabaster in the waning light, almost ghostly from where she was laid peacefully out of the way. Snorting, Reign fetched her discarded bow and slung it over her shoulder before stalking over to one of the wolves and freeing her throwing knives. 

     

                “Not even a day has passed and the Princess is already almost dead,” Andrea clicked her tongue with exasperation. “It would be surprising to have seen otherwise.”

     

                Humming in disconcerting agreement, Kara glanced down at Lena’s deathly pale face and turned to fetch her hunting knife from the throat of the slain wolf while the other two women sorted themselves out. They’d gotten off lightly, with a few shallow scrapes and bruises from being knocked around, but they seemed as exhausted as Kara felt, their tracking leading them on the same wild chase through the woods as she’d taken.

     

                Leaving the wolves for the forest to reclaim, they set about collecting what supplies they could and making a hasty camp atop the large boulders, where they had the potential to avoid being seen. Reign and Andrea’s horses were present though, a tricky situation that would see them all on foot in the morning if they were snatched in the night or would be a dead giveaway to the four fae women perched atop the outcropping. Still, they had to do what they could, leaving the horses to graze below as they scaled the weather-worn boulders, Kara with some difficulty as she carried Lena up with her.

     

                Hands reached down to relieve her of her burden near the top, Andrea and Reign taking Lena’s limp form from Kara’s arms, and Kara scrambled the rest of the way up quickly, distrust rooted in her heart. She found them stretching her out a safe distance from the edge though, and Kara felt a surliness overtake her as she brushed them aside, tearing off her cloak to pillow it beneath Lena’s head.

     

                Andrea and Reign had brought their packs up with them and set about making a small fire with some damp wood they’d scrounged up, their powers making it easier than it had been for Kara below, and Kara shifted closer as she bathed her hands in the warmth of the flames. Watching the two women unpack meagre supplies, she was reluctantly grateful to have them present, even if she didn’t trust them much. Not Reign in her current stare, at least. Even as she watched, Sam pressed the heel of her palm to her temple, face rippling with pain and confusion.

     

                Setting water from the stream to boil, Andrea tossed in a handful of herbs she’d found while gathering wood, steeping them until the air was lightly perfumed by the fragrance of them. They had to share the tea from the canteen Kara dipped in, taking mouthfuls each until it warmed them through, Kara taking the liberty of dribbling some between Lena’s parted lips once it had cooled slightly. Feeling her brow and swallowing thickly with concern as it cut through her dimmed anger, she met the eyes of both women, watching as Reign plucked the feathers from a duck that had been returning to its nest after the fighting and found a throwing knife in its heart. She’d also taken two eggs from the nest, taking life from the forest as they gave back the wolves, and while it was slim pickings, at least they wouldn’t go hungry.

     

                Stewing every part of the duck in the steeped herbs, they waited as it bubbled over the fire, a beacon for everything in the dark as they heard the keening of sly foxes, as large as their horses below, and of other creatures crashing around. More than once, Kara caught the glint of eyes in the trees, predatory birds watching and waiting for their chance to strip the wolves of their rotting flesh. Using one of the damp pieces of wood for the fire to carve a small bowl, Kara handed it off to Andrea first, the most unsuited to venturing through the forest - save for Lena, who was sleeping and wasn’t to be disturbed - and waited for her turn to sip the watery stew from the bubbling pot. While she waited, Kara gave her companions sceptical glances as she tended to her injuries, padding moss against the gash on her thigh and binding it tight with more of her shirt, the other injuries making do with just the moss in light of her dwindling fabric.

     

                “What news?” she eventually asked.

     

                “What news?” Andrea asked. “What news? You cut the Queen’s hand off!”

     

                “A necessary solution to a problem I had no hand in. I would not see her lose her head,” she said, her voice lowering to a mutter as she glanced over at Lena. “Although, in light of what has happened, perhaps I should have left her to her fate.”

     

                “And what has happened?” Reign asked, taking the empty bowl from Andrea and filling it for herself. Her hazel eyes were muddled as her eyelids shuttered, a furrow between her brows. “All I know is the Prince is not dead, as thought, and has brought his rabble of traitors with him.”

     

                Mouth thinning, Kara closed her eyes and inhaled sharply. “That would seem to be the truth of the matter. How did you follow our trail? Last we saw, he had the bank and was struggling to ford the river after I sent the current against them.”

     

                “The fighting grew thick. The Queen sent the bulk of her guard after the Prince-”

     

                “And us?” Kara asked, shoulders tense as her fingers inched towards her hunting knife.

     

                Rolling her eyes, Andrea huddled closer to the fire. “If we meant you ill, we would not have intervened.”

     

                “Then why have you come?”

     

                “You may have cut off her hand but the Queen still lives. Or did when we departed. At any rate, I have no interest in staying at a Court in the midst of a coup.”

     

                “You have defected?” 

     

                “I have a claim to both Courts, as you well know,” Reign said with faint amusement, tapping her brow. “I can already feel her pushing through. And I am a safe emissary for you to travel with - the forest aside.”

                

                “Nevertheless, it’s a cowardly choice. We all know you’re not parted from Lillian’s side unless she wishes a message sent to the Seelie - or spying .”

     

                Andrea let out a quick laugh. “Cowardly? Is the bear cowardly for waiting out the winter while the wolves and the foxes fight for scraps?”

     

                Scoffing, Kara didn’t reply as Reign finished her dinner and passed the empty bowl to Kara. Taking it, Kara filled her bowl and drank it down quickly before refilling it and walking over to Lena. Crouching, she blew on the steaming bowl and gave her wife an appraising look of muddled annoyance and concern before she gently shook her awake.

     

                A thin sigh escaped Lena’s lips as her face furrowed and when Kara shook her insistently, Lena made a low sound of objection at the back of her throat. Unwilling to be disturbed from her rest, injured and bone-leaden, Lena’s eyelashes fluttered as her bottom lip jutted forward. After a moment longer, her eyelids parted and her head lolled before she came back to herself, hissing in pain, wincing as Kara urged her head up and pressed the bowl to her lips.

     

                Making Lena drink it all down, coughing and scowling around the chunks of duck, Kara tucked her wife’s cloak around her tightly, knowing there was nothing else she could do for Lena now. She had the packed and bound arrow wound in her shoulder and that was all Kara could do to treat her until they made it somewhere safe. It wouldn’t be that night.

     

                Claiming the first watch, unwilling to trust her companions despite the truth they’d spoken in their lilting tongue, Kara kept her sword drawn across her lap as she sat near the fire and left the other two women to bed down. Listening to the forest, with its howling wind and murmuring leaves, as if the trees were speaking, the low crash of blundering woodland creatures and predators, the hooting of owls, she was tense and watchful, like the owls on the hunt in the moonlight. 

     

                Eventually, she was disturbed by the shifting movements of someone waking and was relieved of her watch by Reign. Still, she was too stiff to sleep, her mind alert as she waited for an ambush from the hunter who had dragged Lena from the human world, unsure of the stability of the fae in the current circumstances as the Seelie Court hadn’t quite split her in half yet, coaxing out her gentle side. But as she huddled next to her wife, letting her body heat warm Lena as they shared her cloak, Kara heard the hunter softly humming and felt some of the tension bleed out of her past midnight; Sam was shining through and Kara would be grateful to have a friend around. 

     

                In the end, she slept the few remaining hours until late dawn and woke stiff, sore and tired. Rubbing the sleep from her gritty eyes, Kara’s whole body protested as she made herself sit up, disturbing Lena in the process, who woke with more clarity than she had the night before, blinking as she let out a gasp of pain as awareness of her body flooded through her. Glancing at Kara, her attention was snagged by Andrea, who’d taken the last watch and was making some more tea from the stream water and herbs she’d collected that morning, the pot over a fresh fire. 

     

                A panicked sound escaped Lena as she kicked off her cloak and shrank back against Kara’s knees, her wife rising from her haunches to loom over her. Voice gravelly with exhaustion and brittle anger as she met Lena’s pinched face, fraught with shock, Kara raked a hand through her undone braids, caked with blood and dirt and holding the smell of the river she’d waded through the day before to rescue her wife from a mess of her own creation.

     

                “They’re here as allies.”

     

                Confusion clouded her face as she sharply looked up at Kara, Lena staggered to her feet, hand fluttering around her shoulder as she glanced down at her wound, seeming to pale with remembrance. The arrow was gone though and she didn’t know what to make of things as she stood on the boulders, shivering in the chill air of the elements and took in the shadows forms of the wolves as the sun broke over their corpses.

     

                “What the fuck …” was all Lena managed to get out, narrowing her eyes and then turning to give Kara an expectant look.

     

                Avoiding her gaze, Kara stooped and gathered up both of their cloaks, pressing Lena’s to her hands and then fastening her own around her shoulders. Reign raised her eyebrows, hazel eyes mildly inquisitive and warm enough for Kara to know that it was no longer the hunter among them but her kinder half, skinning a rabbit caught during the night. Ignoring her as well, Kara dipped her canteen into the tea and held it out to Andrea first before looking past Lena.

     

                “Come. I must check your wound.”

     

                Lena obediently walked to her side and dropped heavily to the fireside, shuffling closer to the radiating heat. Peeling back the torn edges of Lena’s dress and undoing the bandages, Kara pried the wad of moss back and took in the puckered edges of the weeping wound. The edges of both entry and exit wounds lacked the red of infection so far and Kara breathed a sigh of relief before silently wrapping Lena back up. She didn’t spare a glance for her own wounds, despite the multitude of them, just accepted the canteen from Andrea as she filled it with tea and thrust it to her wife while Sam gutted the rabbit and sighed about the stringy game of it.

     

                Once they’d all had some tea, the rabbit was added to the pot and Kara scaled down the boulders to tend to the horses, leading them to water and washing her hands and face clean in the bracing stream. It invigorated her, the cold sting of it scouring her mind as she tried to have some perspective now that Lena was awake, trying to stamp down her anger until they were somewhere safer. For now, she was as cold as the water she dipped her hands in, feeding from it as she took some small comfort in the knowledge that she was back in her own Court, even if she was stuck in the wilds.

     

                They ate a quick meal, the three of them muttering quietly in their own language as Lena was noticeably excluded, and broke camp with the efficiency of the two women who had spent years traipsing around the forest. Andrea was gentry through and through but had some awareness of the risks at large beyond the confines of any dwellings while Lena was plain ignorant on how to behave, despite knowing the horrors firsthand. Left to her misery, she didn’t speak at all as she shivered near the fire until they were ready to leave.

     

                Due to the unfortunate circumstances of losing their horses, they had to share saddles, Kara depositing her wife on the back of Reign’s black steed before hauling herself up after, while Sam lightly leapt up behind Andrea. It would slow them down but it would be quicker to go at a walk on horseback than to leave them stumbling through the woods in endless drudgery. 

     

                No one spoke for hours, ears pricked for sounds, Sam occasionally leaping from the saddle to scurry up a trunk and scout ahead, returning with little to report. Kara kept Lena’s bow strung, placed across the wife of her lap so she could simultaneously grip the smooth wood and the reins. Kara could feel Lena’s stiffness as she sat in the circle of her arms, stubbornly bad at riding and her heart fluttering lightly as she shivered in her cloak, a cold sweat coating her ashed skin as they rode onwards. Kara knew she needed proper care and silently cursed their slow pace and her wife in equal measure.

     

                It started raining just as the sun had fully risen, a steady patter that broke through the sparse canopy, and spirits were low as they picked a safe path through the trees, all of them taut as they strained their ears for sounds. The sudden flutter of wings startled them at one point as a goldfinch took of from its nest, quickly shot down by Kara’s swift arrow, her heart racing as she slowed the horse back down again, Sam and Andrea reining in their own as the urgent need to flee died. It tense silence was awful and even though Kara had spent endless hours in the forest, the growing austerity of the encroaching winter made her skin prickle with unease, the notion of how ill-prepared they were troublesome.

     

                It was late morning by the time they came upon the safe holdings she’d remembered, a dead-end gully that wove through the root system of old trees that had grown around mossy rocks. It was a small dwelling, two dozen Earthfolk burrowing into the mud and rock, trees moulded into shape by their capable skill as they built their lives around the forest, rather than the human way of destroying what stood in the way. 

     

                Swinging down from her horse, Kara left Lena seated as she approached three fae archers hidden amongst the overhead web of roots masking the entrance to the small fort. Hands bared and held aloft, she introduced herself and spoke of their need, one of them finding her familiar enough and trusting her honest words as they were led through the passage. Kara took the bridle of her horse and led Lena along on foot, emerging into the comfortably woody home of the busy fae as they went about their lives.

     

                Two men were weaving baskets from thin willow switches, a woman was skinning the hide of a monstrously large deer, its hide like dark moss, antlers spanning almost the width of the dead-end, hardpacked earthen clearing they’d emerged into. Despite having nothing to trade, they were provided with all that they needed, as was the way of their people, freely given with the knowledge that they would want for nothing if ever they begged of Kara. 

     

                They didn’t have horses to spare though so as they were handed full saddlebags, they had to add them to the weight of two riders per horse but Kara felt more secure as they departed after a quick lunch. Lena had been given a healing tea of willow bark and valerian that left her drowsy as she slumped against Kara in the saddle, slightly feverish and weakened from her injuries. 

     

                Saddlesore and grim, soaked to their bones as the hours dragged on and the rain grew heavier, they passed through the unchanging landscape, similar trees and rocky formations, valleys and slopes and streams passing by without it feeling like they were getting anywhere. Kara had never spent much time south of the river crossing so she wasn’t as familiar with the passing landscape, and with the grey cloud cover masking the sun she had to rely on Sam to guide them, Reign’s political forays into the Seelie Court lending them the knowledge of where to go.

     

                Afternoon dragged towards dusk without a safe haven in sight to set up camp but they were fortunate to be relatively alone in the woods. It was only the beginning of winter but already some of the creatures had retreated south to the marginally warmer climate, away from the distant haze of the mountains, already bearing snow. Of course, they didn’t let their guard down at all, weapons held in fingers stiffly locked into place around the hilts and grips. The sky was purple, the land a silhouette as they passed the white sage and ancient oaks, when Kara felt a prickle of unease.

                

                Through the creaking of branches and the wail of the wind through the bare forest, she strained her ears to pick up the faintest sound of hooves behind them. Eyes flashing to Sam’s face, she saw a flicker that corroborated her suspicions.

     

                “We’re being followed,” Sam murmured.

     

                They urged the horses faster, although Kara feared how much more they could endure of the relentless pace, the light already failing them with no suitable hiding spot for them to camp, and now with the four sets of hooves behind them, Kara was worried they’d be fleeing all night or caught if not. The latter was correct as they rode hard for the next few miles, the sounds of pursuit growing louder, closer. 

     

                When Kara judged them to be no more than a mile behind them, their pursuers pace faster than theirs in light of the four women riding double, she shouted to Sam and then forced Lena’s stiff fingers around the reins. Slinging the strung bow across her back, Kara shifted into a crouch on the horse’s back, her nimble agility allowing her to keep her balance for a moment as she judged the trees they stripped past, timing their pace.

     

                “Keep riding,” she ordered Lena before launching herself off the back of the horse.

     

                Using the trunk of the tree she’d aimed for, Kara pushed herself up to the lowest branch, one hand closing over rough bark before she gritted her teeth and pulled herself up. The horses carried on and she ducked and lithely jumped from branch to branch as she waited for their pursuers to catch up. Streaking through the gloom of the forest, Kara slipped her hunting knife free of its sheath and held it tightly in her grasp as she ran along the boughs of a thick oak and heard the heartbeats, sharp breaths and hooves coming thundering below.

     

                Inhaling sharply, Kara ran to the end of the branch and then leapt through the twigs and leaves with snapping and rustling and the cold bite of air and scratches against her skin as she hurtled downwards. She’d timed it well and aimed true, striking into the side of the second rider and knocking them both out of the saddle, landing in a painful heap. Feeling her injuries flare with white-hot pain, Kara swallowed the metallic taste of blood as she rolled the woman off her and climbed on top, the keen edge of her knife going to her throat.

     

                “Two days you’ve had me scouring the woods for you and this is how I am to be greeted?” Alex rasped, a shaky laugh escaping her as her own hands went limp at her side, flames guttering in her palms.

     

                “Alex,” Kara breathed with relief, wrenching away her knife as her body went slack.

     

                Quickly climbing off her sister, Kara shot to her feet and sheathed her knife, glancing around to make sense of what was happening. A short way through the trees, she could hear voices and was quick to sprint through the trees, finding Lena flat on her back, unhorsed again, and Kelly on her knees with Andrea and Sam bickering back and forth. Horses milled about and Kara recognised two of them as the ones she and Lena had lost the day before. 

     

                “It’s alright,” Kara called out, Alex following behind her, grumbling as she rolled her shoulder. “It’s my kin, seeking us.”

     

                “When you didn’t show at the bridge yesterday to cross, we scouted up and down the river. Kelly came with me; James is with Querl and Nia heading north.”

     

                As the tension defused, Kara turned and wrapped her sister in a tight hug before touching their foreheads together and smiling. “It’s good to see you.”

     

                Squeezing her arm before pulling back, Alex grinned. “And you. Although, you have seen better days.”

     

                “It will be a long tale to tell.”

     

                “I’m dying to hear all about the Unseelie Court. And your … interesting companions,” Alex said, her eyes sliding to the pair of women. “Sam.”

     

                “Alex.”

     

                “Does the Queen care so much for my sister and her daughter’s safe return that she sends you once more?”

     

                “I’m here at my own behest,” Sam said with a thin smile. “I’m sure my Queen will not take kindly to me stretching the confines of my oaths to her but as I told your sister, I am half of each Court so may travel as I see fit.”

     

                Alex said nothing of Andrea and Kara hugged Kelly, murmuring quietly as they greeted each other warmly, before she turned her attention to Lena. Squatting as she pressed a hand to her shoulder, her skin holding a waxy sheen to the greyness of it. She wasn’t faring well and Kara’s mouth turned down at the corners.

     

                “We shall have to tie you to your horse if we’re to have any hope of you staying in the saddle,” she grumbled, fingers encircling Lena’s bicep and urging her to her feet.

     

                “I’m so … tired,” Lena wearily replied, her voice resigned and thin.

     

                “Is she well?” Kelly asked, concern shining in her dark eyes.

     

                “An arrow wound. We have both endured much these last two days. There is not much to do until we reach home.”

     

                Alex glanced up at the darkening sky and then at the ground of unlikely travelling companions, her mouth thinning grimly. “Home is yet miles away but we can cover a few more before we rest this night.”

     

                With the fear of pursuit put to rest and their number added to, making it harder to slip through the forest unnoticed but adding two more skilled fighters, they set off at a brisk trot, each to their own horse. Kara rode closely behind Lena, eyes drilling into her back as she watched her sway precariously in her saddle, tensed in anticipation of her coming unseated again. Her frustration with her wife hadn’t lessened as the days had passed but Kara kept her feelings to herself, waiting for an appropriate time to let it out. Travelling through the forest at night with eyes and ears about was not it.

     

                They rode well past when true night fell, the forest pitch-black, their horses’ snorts and scuffing hooves filling the silence with the sharp keening of the wind through the trees. All of them were tense and tired, stiff and cold as they plodded onwards, and when Alex finally called a halt, all of them were eager for the rest. Feet landing on the damp carpet of rotting leaves, Kara walked to the side of Lena’s mount and looked up into the haggard face of her wife with a sliver of pity cutting through her chest; this was harder on Lena than anyone else, so ill-suited to the cruelty of the Courts, and Kara had to press her lips hard together to stop herself from making a snide comment on her acts.

     

                Bedding down in the shelter of a leaning sheet of rock, damming the worst of the wind as it blew down from the mountains in the north, they built up a fire to keep away the smaller creatures and picketed the horses nearby. With their saddlebags back, Kara and Lena provided some of their missing supplies with Alex and Kelly supplying more, making for better fare than they’d had the night before. 

     

                Huddled around the warmth of the fire, they all sipped a strong tea and ate a heartier stew with bread before splitting a few late autumn apples. Alex had a flask of honey wine that they all shared around, a few mouthfuls each, and Kara felt more at peace with her sister at her side. Alex insisted on taking the first watch as they started to stretch out where they could, Kara making a bed up for Lena with their bedrolls and her cloak before she sat beside her sister and they spoke quietly until all was said. Grim and worried, Alex said little and eventually Kara went to her own rest beside her wife, sharing her cloak and feeling warmed through from the fire and Lena’s body heat.

     

                She wasn’t disturbed for a watch and rose with the dawn. Lena’s grey face bore two spots of colour in her cheeks as she sweated through her clothes, fever inevitably setting in, and it was all Kara could do to make her drink some tea and get her in the saddle after she refused anything to eat. Despite it being harder on the horse and slowing them down, she was reluctant to leave Lena to ride alone that day, her concern for her cutting through any other feelings at the present.

     

                It was a long, trudging day through brackish waters and mud, through stagnant, marshy land with rotting trees and evident signs of old slaughters in the patches of clover and moss and wilting weeds that covered long-dead bodies. Lena was barely conscious through most of it, head lolling against Kara’s shoulder as they brought up the rear, the long line of them snaking through the forest as the mountains loomed closer with each passing hour.

     

                They stopped for a brief lunch, where Lena went without once more, and pressed onwards, Alex leading them to their mother’s home, a place for them to rest in safety for as long as they needed. Still, the day grew bitter as they passed into colder territory, the wind turning, carrying eddying blasts of sleet as they rose up the sides of densely packed hills and down the steep, winding valleys of the forest. The light failed as the ground started to turn rocky, the landscape familiar from Kara’s youth, spent playing in the reaching fingers of the mountain range’s foothills where Eliza’s home resided.

     

                She could see some of the tension bleed from her sister’s shoulders far ahead of her, leading from the front of the line of their party, and Kara felt a similar relief at the thought of safety. They still had hours to go yet, the spreading ridges of the foothills spanning miles and miles of increasingly steep paths through the sheer cliff faces of the narrow passes. They would be crowded with trees and boulders, streams already giving over to ice as the winter came on quickly in the higher altitude of the looming mountains but they would press on through the night until they arrived at their destination.

     

                A storm fell as they wound through a narrow pass along a rocky arm of the foothills, their view limited to their party cast in the warm glow of buffeting torches held aloft by Alex and Sam. A light snow started to fall, the chill burrowing into them, clouds blotting out any moonlight as they were led almost blindly through the dangerous terrain. They were not so high up where life couldn’t thrive though, Eliza’s holdings not far from the ground, although the path there was winding and slow going, and they passed through the safety of many bare trees, hiding their passing from the sight of any predators prowling the night.

     

                Eventually, they took a switch-back path up a sheer cliff face and came to a stop outside the lip of an elaborately carved wall of rock. Motifs of wind and birds and elegantly twisting spires with holes carved into them greeted Kara with a buoying feeling of delight in her chest; it had been so long since she’d visited her home and her adoptive mother, her responsibilities for her own holdings keeping her further south-east in the warmer months and north beyond the mountains in the winter. It was usually passing through and on the solstices that Kara spent most of her time with her mother and she was sad to have lost out on two of them - although, that was debatable now, with the way the truce hung in shreds between the Courts.

     

                “We shall see to the horses,” Alex said as she dismounted, jerking her chin towards Kara with a faint furrow between her eyebrows. “Tend to your wife.”

     

                Nodding gravely, Kara swung down and eased Lena down into her arms, eyelashes fluttering and a small sound of complaint escaping Lena’s lips. She opened her eyes then, a muddled green as she looked around, confusion pinching her face. When her eyes met Kara’s, she quickly looked away, taking in the carved facade of the dwelling with a gentle look of awe in the slackening of her mouth.

     

                “Where are we?” she hoarsely asked, more than she’d said all day.

     

                “Can you walk or do you wish for me to carry you?”

     

                Struggling in Kara’s arms, Lena made her preference clear, but when Kara set her on her feet, her knees buckled and she started to sag towards the snow-covered ground. Sighing, Kara swept her up into her arms again and strode forward, the thin crust of snow and frost breaking beneath her bare feet; it would almost be time to wear shoes.

     

                Entering the halls of her mother, Kara found the way dark, torches not yet lit, but she knew the path well enough, walking down the wide hallway and navigating the hallways parting off it with ease until she came to a room where Eliza kept herbs. It was a small room, comfortably small despite the frigid stone walls, floors and arched ceiling, all of it beautifully carved like the rest of the halls. The wind whistled through the artfully carved holes bored through the rock to create a melodic sound, not unlike flutes or other wind instruments, and Kara felt a sense of peace in her bones as she set Lena down before the empty hearth and set about making a fire.

     

                Once the flames were crackling merrily, the smell of cedar and apple wood a comforting scent as heat flooded the small chamber, Kara squatted at her wife’s side and rid her of her damp cloak, sodden and snow-dusted as it thawed in the warmth of the fire. Rising, she draped it over the back of a chair and dragged her damp hair out of her face, the tips of her ears pink from the cold, lips chapped and the circles beneath her eyes darker than they’d ever been. Kara would have liked to sleep where she was standing.

     

                A deep silence filled the chamber and Lena eventually looked up at Kara, a cowed look to her sallow face, her shoulders slumped wearily, eyes fever-bright. “Thank you.”

     

                A muscle twitched in Kara’s jaw and she didn’t respond as she stood stiffly a few feet away, warming herself as she considered what to do next. They needed to tend to their wounds, obviously, she needed to speak to her mother, get some sleep, a good meal, a hot bath. She didn’t even know where to begin; she just knew she didn’t want to speak to her wife right then.

     

                “Are you ignoring me? I know you must be angry but if it’s any consolation … I’m sorry for what I did.”

     

                Her feeble words snapped something inside Kara, whose blue eyes sharpened, back stiffened, and morals and dutiful sensibilities rankled as she whipped her gaze down to Lena, piercing enough to chill her wife. Swallowing thickly, Lena opened her mouth again but was cut off by Kara’s hot response as her bottled-up thoughts and feeling spilt forth.

     

                “Don’t apologise. Don’t even speak. Better yet, don’t even look at me. I cannot bear the sight of you without it angering me. How many times must you behave recklessly until you stop this selfish nonsense? Is our spilt blood not enough to satisfy you? You have almost died several times at your own foolishness, without any regard for how that will affect anyone else. What that means for me, my life.”

     

                “I was doing this to get away from you,” Lena hotly replied as she staggered to her feet, her cheeks red from the scolding and fever alike. “And I never asked you to defend me, to risk your life for me.”

     

                “And what do you think would happen if I let them cut you down without lifting my sword? Do you think I would be spared on account of my lack of involvement? I would be dead alongside you.”

     

                “You cut off her hand! You started this; I was trying to end it.”

     

                Kara scoffed and reached out, causing Lena to flinch back before gentle fingertips grazed the purple bruises on Lena’s neck, lining up to the sharp points of Lillian’s nails where she’d gripped her tightly. “She was going to kill you. No threats this time, only action. Would you have had me stand by idly? You cast suspicion onto me. If it is to be war then it’s your fault. ”

     

                Scowling as she pressed a finger to her sternum, Lena rankled. “My fault? You’ve been at war for centuries. Longer. You think this marriage was ever anything more than a ploy for her to buy more time to figure out how to win? I will not feel guilty for something that was inevitable in the first place. All I did was find a way to free us while you sat around waiting for winter so you could go home again. Well, I can’t go home-”

     

                “This again,” Kara scoffed, running a hand over her face.

     

                “Yes, this. I can’t go home but that doesn’t mean I have to be content with being manipulated and threatened into obedience. And now I’m free to do what I want, start over.”

     

                Turning away from her, Kara grabbed Lena’s damp cloak and bundled it up, thrusting it against her chest. “Go on then. Away with you. You’re not welcome here.”

     

                Spluttering, a look of shock flashed across Lena’s face. “Wha- I-”

     

                “You wanted your freedom; now you have it. At the expense of innumerable lives. So, go.”

     

                Red cheeks blanching, Lena opened and closed her mouth, a scoff of disbelief working its way up her throat. “You’re kicking me out? It’s the middle of the night!”

     

                “Now you want to be with me?” Kara asked, her face flushed pink with anger as she scowled, her pretty features only enhanced by the colour in her cheeks, the brightness of her eyes, firelight turning her hair amber. “When it is convenient for you. When I can keep you safe again. You cannot have it both ways. You have no thought for anyone but yourself, of doing what serves a purpose to you. I mean it, Lena, I have no desire for you to be here if you’re going to make trouble. Not here.”

     

                Her voice grew sharp at the end and they were barely a foot apart, Kara still pressing Lena’s filthy cloak to her chest, Lena pale with disbelief, her fraying emotions getting the better of her, as exhausted, injured and confused as she was. It hadn’t gone to plan and she did feel guilty but she hadn’t expected to be thrown out into the night by her furious wife. Could she even call Kara that anymore? The truce had definitely fallen apart the moment Kara had cut Lillian’s hand off, further turmoil with Lex throwing things into chaotic disarray, so it was safe to say that she no longer had to consider herself beholden to the marriage she’d been involuntarily subjected to. 

     

                “So that’s it? You’re going to throw me to the wolves?”

     

                “You threw yourself to the wolves. I could’ve left you out there to die but I didn’t-”

     

                “What, because you’re so noble . Please, tell me again how honourable you are, I haven’t heard enough-”

     

                “You can scoff all you want but I wouldn’t want you in my foxhole in the dead of winter.”

     

                “I wouldn’t want you if we were the last two people in this forest.”

                

                “I’d rather cut my heart out of my chest than willingly want you.”

     

                “If you have to insult someone twice then you’ve already failed to hurt them,” Lena shot back, her voice wavering as her shoulder ached terribly.

     

                “You’re your own worst enemy, Lena. I don’t have to insult you; you already hurt yourself deeper than I ever could with your embarrassing attempts to play the game of politics. You are clumsy, like a child. You are insolent, like a child. You are ignorant, like a child. The best thing that could have happened would have been if I’d left you to the forest when you came back, to spare us all the pain of enduring you.”

     

                Lena’s blood ran cold at her words, her mouth opening and closing soundlessly as her eyes stung with vicious tears. Clenching her teeth together, her face hardened with anger but the wounded look of betrayal in her green eyes told the truth of the matter as she swallowed painfully and grabbed a fistful of the cloak pressed to her chest and thrust it back towards Kara. Looking surprised at her own audacity, Kara stumbled back a step and Lena kept going, pushing her again as hot tears spilt over, wetting her cheeks.

     

                “It’s a good thing you’re cursed; anyone who’s unlucky enough to be loved by you won’t have to suffer for long,” Lena thickly snapped, a low blow that made Kara’s scowl falter as doe-eyed pain took its place.

     

                “You never had to worry - it never would have been you.”

     

                Wind buffeted them apart then before Kara could advance on Lena, a sharp gust that tore them away from each other, staggering a few steps from the force. Swaying unsteadily as her weak limbs tried to find their balance, her cloak trailing to the floor in her limp arms, Lena was aware of another voice cutting through the tense argument.

     

                “Enough! This is a house of peace.”

     

                She blinked back the film of tears limning her waterline and took in the sight of a blonde woman with sky blue eyes that were piercing as she looked between both women. She wore a snow-soaked robe the colour of fog, hanging in fluid folds with whorls wrought like air and Lena realised she had torn them apart with her ability, with the very air they breathed. 

     

                Kara was speechless for a moment, still caught up in her anger as she stared at the woman. After regaining some of her composure, she moved fluidly across the room and sank to her knees, head bowed as her damp blonde hair cascaded around her, speaking breathlessly.

     

                “Mother.”

     

                Blinking in surprise, Lena was silent and rooted to the spot as she watched the blonde woman cup her daughter’s cheek and Kara covered it with her own hand, lifting her eyes to meet her gaze. Rising to her feet, Kara engulfed the other woman in a hug, holding her tightly, and Lena was struck by their likeness, even knowing Kara’s mother was dead. Her adoptive mother looked more like Kara than Alex, and they were even of a height as Kara stepped back and faced her mother.

     

                “I have been in observance for three days for the changing of the seasons,” Eliza softly sighed, a worn look on her face as her shoulders slumped. “And I come home to a quarrel? Kara Zor-El, you should know better than to speak such unkindness, especially to one's own wife. Have shame - both of you.”

     

                Kara’s cheeks coloured at the berating and she hung her head again, the tips of her ears turning red where it parted her sheets of tangled hair, and Lena found herself blanching as the woman’s eyes turned their attention to her. Quickly focusing her gaze on the ground, she wrung her cloak in her hands nervously, a lump lodged in her throat. 

     

                “Forgive us,” Kara murmured, “it has been … a difficult few days.”

     

                “You are hurt.”

     

                Eyes flashing up to her mother’s face, Kara followed her line of sight to Lena, who was still avoiding eye contact. It wasn’t until the woman was in front of her that she was forced to look up, shrinking back slightly, her knuckles turning white as she clutched her cloak. 

     

                “There isn’t enough air in your blood,” Eliza murmured, her fingers reaching out but stopping short of touching Lena before her eyes dropped to her shoulder.

     

                “I tended it as best I could while fleeing,” Kara murmured. “The arrow went cleanly through her after she fell off her horse; there was a lot of blood.”

     

                Gentle hands fell on her good shoulder and Lena found herself being shepherded to a low wooden stool. “Come. Sit.”

     

                Glancing over her shoulder, the woman looked at her daughter. “Fetch clean water and then you may assist.”

     

                “I will fetch the water and then tend to my own injuries.”

     

                “You will tend to your wife first.”

     

                Although her mother’s tone was gentle, it left no room for argument and Kara bristled slightly before her shoulders caved and she stalked out of the room. The cloak was slowly freed from her grasp and Lena’s gaze turned from the open doorway to blink at the woman kneeling in front of her, so close and unfamiliar that Lena’s pulse jumped. The split seams of her dress made it easy for the woman to reveal the mass of torn linen Kara had used to bind the wound, her movements careful, mindful of the throbbing pain in Lena’s shoulder.

     

                “So … you are Lena,” the woman murmured, her eyes flitting up to take in the bruised and bloody face of her daughter-in-law. 

     

                Making a frayed sound of agreement at the back of her throat, Lena’s eyelids shuttered and she tried not to wince as the woman peeled back the bandages holding bloody moss to the arrow wound, the clumps coming free with it, the coppery smell of blood perfuming the air. 

     

                “I am Eliza.”

     

                “Her mother.”

     

                “Yes. She has told you of me?”

     

                “Yes.”

     

                Nodding, Eliza peeled aside more moss and then rose to her feet, moving behind Lena to remove the moss at the back as well. Kara was back a minute later with a basin of water, steam rising from the surface, before she rummaged around in a few drawers and jars in the rood before approaching Lena with the fragrant scent of herbs wafting from the basin. Steam made her skin prickle as Kara knelt in front of her and motioned for the water to rise. She pressed the hot water against the entrance wound and Lena baulked, a hiss of pain escaping her as she tried to move away.

     

                Eliza was behind her though and clamped a hand on Lena’s good shoulder, keeping her seated. Her other hand tenderly stroked her dark hair and Lena let out a soft whimper as Kara cleaned out the wound, pink water streaking down her chest and into the ruins of her dress, flecks of moss and dirt dotting her skin. It hurt fiercely, her eyes stinging with pain as her body went taut and she tried to endure it without complaint. The dull ache had been preferable to the tending of it and Lena thought she might vomit into her lap, already light-headed and sickly warm, despite how cold she’d been before.

     

                Kara had to repeat the process on the back and then flooded water through the wound and Eliza clicked her tongue as she gently pressed around the bruise entry wound, spotting a splinter and directing Kara to flush it out. Once the wound was clear, pink water splashing into the fire in the hearth as a cloud of steam billowed out, Eliza turned from the flames with a kettle wrapped in roughspun cloth and poured boiling water into a pot of herbs. Letting it steep for a moment, she bid Lena drink it while Kara threaded sinew onto a fishbone hook behind her and sank to a knee.

     

                “This will hurt,” she muttered to Lena, still sounding sullen and affronted, and pushed the point of the needle through the edge of the exit wound.

     

                Lena saw black, sour bile rising up her throat as she choked it down with a gasp, her lips going bloodless and thin as she closed her eyes. The herbs only helped a little and she would have preferred unconsciousness to the piercing pain of the needle pushing in and out as the edges of the exit wound were pulled together. She only did the back to make sure the wound could heal properly and, eventually, Kara finished and Eliza mixed honey with herbs into a wooden bowl and then pasted it over the entry and exit wounds to keep it from festering before applying pieces of linen to the honey and then slowly binding Lena’s shoulder with clean lengths of bandages. 

     

                Bloody face covered in sweat as she swayed unsteadily on the stool, Lena ran her sleeve over her face, aching for bed. It had been an arduous few days and this had been too much, all of her strength fleeing her as she’d been stitched back together. Taking a moment to collect herself, Lena was about to stagger to her feet when Eliza stopped her.

     

                Shifting another stool beside Lena’s, Eliza pointed her daughter to it and then set the bowl of steaming water on Lena’s lap with a clean cloth. “And now it is your turn.”

     

                Confusion gave way to doubt as Lena looked up at her, holding the cloth and stammering slightly. “But- I don’t know how to heal.”

     

                “Her injuries need bathing - I assume you can wash?” Eliza asked in that calm but firm manner of hers. “She is your wife so you will tend to her wounds. Marriage is about caring for one another.”

     

                Lena kept her mouth closed on her opinions of their marriage as she softly sighed and dipped the cloth in the remaining water, squeezing out the excess and glowering at Kara as their eyes met. Looking as displeased as Lena, Kara quietly scoffed and scooted her stool closer, their knees almost touching as she deftly rolled up a torn sleeve to reveal the gash in her bicep. Dabbing at the crust of dried blood, Lena felt her pulse in her throat as she carefully cleaned it out, trying not to disturb the developed scabs too much. She was instructed on how to bind Kara’s fingers with a splint of ash wood, keeping them straight until they mended, and wiped the grazes and cuts that peppered her with as much gentleness as she could manage.

     

                Then there was the cut on Kara’s thigh, which her wife was forced to bare, tanned skin smeared with old blood, the wound a nasty thing that was warm to touch around the site of it. Eliza helped her with that one, the fragrant herbs rinsing it clean, the needle shaking in Lena’s clumsy fingers as she unsteadily forced it through the edge of the deep gash. She was sick instead, heaving up what little was in her stomach as she sloshed the bowl of water everywhere and lurched to her feet, excusing herself from the task of stitching Kara up. 

     

                Shockingly pale and horribly faint, Lena paced the hallway outside as Eliza finished tending to her daughter in her stead, standing in the cold hallway as she looked at the delicate stonework of the ribbed ceiling and pillars, clouds and columns of wind currents. She would have gone elsewhere but Lena had no clue where she was within the elegantly fashioned halls carved high up in the face of the cliffside. 

     

                She stopped pacing when footsteps padded towards the open archway of the door and watched as Kara emerged. Her expression was drawn with pain and she looked as exhausted as Lena - perhaps even more so - barely sparing her a glance as she stepped outside with her mother following behind.

     

                “I need rest,” Kara murmured, looking back over her shoulder at Eliza. “If you will excuse me.”

     

                “We shall talk more in the morning,” Eliza agreed, laying a hand on Kara’s shoulder and squeezing gently. “Your room is made up. As is the room beside it.”

     

                Her eyes slid to Lena, who raked a hand through her hair, feeling in desperate need of a bath and a good night’s sleep but still irate from her argument with Kara. It had simmered in light of the treatment and beration of her would-be mother-in-law but Lena had too much pride to be cast out and beg to stay.

     

                “Thank you but I won’t be needing a room,” she curtly replied. “It’s been made clear I’m not welcome here.”

     

                “The wind may bitterly howl but the wind can also be a warm caress. Such is the temperament of all creatures. Do not take offence to words said in haste. As it is, it is not for others to decide who is and isn’t welcome in my home.”

     

                Kara shifted uncomfortably and Lena fiddled with her fingers as she stared at the engraved eaves above Eliza’s head, stone birds of every species wrought in near lifelike skill. Neither of them spoke and after a moment Eliza pointedly cleared her throat.

     

                “I would have you make amends if you are staying beneath my roof; all quarrels are to be left beyond the threshold of these halls.”

     

                Letting out a soft sigh, Kara nodded and kissed her mother’s cheek goodnight before gesturing for Lena to follow her. Ducking her head politely, Lena folded her arms over her chest and lagged a few steps behind as she stared sulkily at Kara’s back, her own stinging from the stitches just above her shoulder blade, her left side so stiff she could barely stand to move it. She kept any complaints behind shut lips and walked through the eerily quiet hallways as the wind howled through, a strange beauty to the music of it, the wonderfully sculpted holes scattered throughout the home that made it sound like woodwind instruments.

     

                Stopping outside an archway covered by a gauzy curtain, Kara gestured to it with a sour look on her face, brooding with pursed lips. Clearing her throat rather reluctantly, she faced Lena but didn’t look her in the eye, as Lena likewise avoided Kara’s.

     

                “Forgive me, I did not mean what I said. It has been a trying few days and worry brought forth my temper.”

     

                “Don’t apologise,” Lena haughtily replied. “I would think less of you if you retreated because your mom told you to. You meant it, so mean it.”

     

                Face darkening with annoyance, Kara’s mouth thinned and they stood in silence for a moment, both of them resentful and peevish, sheepish and awkward, until Kara brushed through the gauzy curtain of Lena’s room and built up the crackling fire set in the fireplace. Brushing aside the curtain, Lena stood on the threshold of an austere room, everything carved out of the bedrock of the mountain, from the slab a mattress and thick quilts rested on, the fireplace and the row of shelves. The only real furniture was a trunk set in the corner and a wooden stool but it was comfortable and as beautifully carved as the rest of the place, growing warmer with the fire as well. 

     

                Dusting off her hands, Kara rose to her feet and gave Lena a level stare for a moment before she stalked back over to the door and twisted past her, ensuring they didn’t touch. Pausing a moment longer as she held the curtain aside with one hand, Kara’s mouth twisted with annoyance.

     

                “Sleep well.”

     

                Lena didn’t reply, her cheeks flushing with embarrassment, her shoulder hurting more than any pain she could remember, and she hugged the ruins of her dress to herself as she stood in the orange glow of the room for a moment. With a weary sigh, she sat on the edge of the bed and ran a hand over her face and through her hair, regretting so much and feeling so stupid as she blundered through the unknown and made things worse. Lena was finding she had a knack for that, almost as good as her knack for plants. 

     

                As much as she ached to shed her wet dress and wrap herself up in the thick, warm quilt, Lena couldn’t bring herself to do, couldn’t bring herself to stay, her pride and embarrassment eclipsing all other sense. She waited a short while, thinking Kara would be asleep by then, and slipped out of the room on quiet feet. 

     

                Hot and weak, she stumbled through the hallways with no sense of direction and must have wandered for almost an hour before she found the wide hallways leading to the exit, feeling the frigid gust of the wind outdoors sweeping down it with the musical sound of the halls. Hugging her arms to herself, she forged onwards with the idea in mind to steal a horse and whatever supplies were still in her pack and make herself scarce, getting as far from the fallout of what she’d helped orchestrate, as was her original plan.

     

                Once she reached the dark mouth of the hallway, Lena was almost buffeted back by the gale assaulting the side of the foothill, her legs shaking and the air snatched from her lungs. Stepping outside, she concentrated on taking deep, bruising lungfuls of the bitter air, like a knife down her throat as her breath plumed white into the dark, and took a moment to gather her thoughts and cobble together a plan.

     

                “Ah, she was right - you are predictable.”

     

                Lena jumped at the voice to her left, softly swearing beneath her breath as she whirled towards it, shifting back a step to put space between her and the shadowed figure. Five fingertips burst into flames and illuminated Alex’s wolffish smile as she pushed off the wall of the cliff face.

     

                Disgruntled at how easily she spooked, Lena hitched her pack higher on her right shoulder. “How?”

     

                “She said you’d try to leave.”

     

                “She told me to go. It’s not predictable to follow orders.”

     

                “When have you ever done what you were told?”

     

                Opening and closing her mouth, Lena had no answer for that but bristled indignantly at the insinuation. But her umbrage quickly faltered, the line of her mouth wavering, and a ragged gasp escaped Lena as her eyes filled with hot tears, spilling over and running down her cheeks. Hanging her head as hot shame washed over her, Lena hurriedly wiped at her cheeks and heard the other woman sigh at the display of tears.

     

                “I will not comfort you with empty words diminishing your foolishness but … you were easily manipulated and that is no fault of yours.”

     

                “What do you know about it?” Lena sharply retorted.

     

                “I know that I would have reacted similarly if I did not know the truth, as you did not. One can only learn the bite of fire by sticking one’s hand in the flames. Next time, heed her warnings; she does not nag you for the sake of it, only to keep you safe.”

     

                “I know that. But has she considered that I want to make my own decisions, my own mistakes? I don’t want her to rescue me. I just- I want her to leave me alone. I want all of you to just … leave me alone.”

     

                “The lone wolf dies in winter.”

     

                Scoffing, Lena shivered, a hard set to her jaw as she shifted from foot to foot, the cold of the snow numbing the soles of her feet, fighting to stifle the chatter of her teeth. “The lone wolf gets a bit of peace and quiet.”

     

                “Then perhaps you should seek out somewhere to be alone with your thoughts, as your wife does.”

     

                “Where is she?”

     

                “At the lake.”

     

                “The lake?”

     

                “She misses the water. 

     

                “In this weather?”

     

                “In all weather, as you would miss the forest if you were forced to live up here. As you will once you make it to her winter residence.”

     

                Lips twisting ruefully, Lena frowned. “I don’t think I’ll be making it there.”

     

                “You will. It will not always be this way.”

     

                “Oh, yeah? And how do you know that?”

     

                “Go to bed, Lena,” Alex gently urged her, ignoring her question. “All will be well with the sunrise.”

    Chapter 17

                As tired as she was, Kara woke early, before the sun had even peeked over the horizon beyond the carved halls of the mountain hold, neatly making her bed and poking through the untouched belongings she kept there. Handling a large shell, she ran her thumb over the ridges of it and breathed in the smell of salt and sand with the wistful longing of someone who hadn’t seen the sea in far too long. She would have been there already if things had been normal, beating the early winter snows in the mountain passes, which would undoubtedly make their onward approaching journey more difficult. 

     

                Flipping through the pages of a well-loved wood-bound book on the tides and currents, she listened to the light flutter of her wife’s heartbeat next door and snapped the book shut with a sigh. Setting it down on the shelf, she hesitated before stepping out of her room and pausing outside the door to the room beside hers. 

     

                Pushing aside the gauzy curtain offering her wife some privacy, Kara took in the shadowed figure of her sleeping by the smouldering embers of the fire. Lena shifted and Kara froze for a moment, thinking she’d disturbed her, that she’d been caught spying, but Lena just moved restlessly, her voice a low murmuring whine as she kicked the sheets off. Softly sighing to herself, Kara quietly padded inside, a faint limp to her gait as she crossed over to Lena, the chill of the room seeping into the soles of her feet.

     

                Pausing at her bedside, Kara reached down to pull the sheets back over her and paused at the sheen of sweat on Lena’s skin. Reaching down, Kara pressed the back of her hand against her brow and frowned, a knife of worry cutting through her. Pulling the sheets back and turning to the fire, Kara completely banked the embers and cast a worried glance at Lena’s restless form before stalking out of the room with purpose.

     

                Her thigh pained her more than her other injuries and she had a pounding ache in her head but Kara hobbled through the halls for Eliza’s usual haunts, barely pausing in the door of the wide kitchens at the sound of voices, finding Alex and Kelly sitting by the cavernous hearth as torrents of condensed wind whisked plates around, sacks of flour and knives. Pressing onwards, it didn’t take her much longer to find her mother in one of the outer chambers, narrow arched windows carved into the mountainside overlooking the sweeping forest beyond as rain fought its way through the gaps.

     

                The room was draughty but a fire was lit, taking the edge off it as she stepped inside, disturbing Eliza from her peaceful reading in one of her favourite rooms. Kara had spent many days much like this reading at her mother’s feet, drinking tea and lamenting about being stuck inside beneath the weight of so much stone, so far from the glinting slivers of rivers and streams visible through the windows. 

     

                “Mother.”

     

                Glancing over her shoulder, Eliza’s face softened with a pleased smile and she climbed to her feet, arms held out for her daughter. Kara met her halfway and Eliza gently cupped her cheeks in her palms before kissing one and wrapping her in a hug.

     

                “Oh, it is good to have you in these halls once more. You have been sorely missed.”

     

                Smiling weakly, Kara nodded tiredly as she returned the hug, the comfort of it a balm to the parts of her that had been knotted with tension and unease for the entirety of autumn. But now it was past them and Kara felt some of her concerns slip away, although there was a lingering feeling of dread over the fallout of the events that had transpired. 

     

                Sighing heavily, she drew back and her mouth thinned as she held onto her mother’s arms, worry evident in her blue eyes. “She is feverish.”

     

                Nodding, Eliza gave her shoulder a quick pat. “I shall see to her now.”

     

                Gratitude flushed through her but Kara was stiff and solemn, rubbing her brow, shifting her weight restlessly as her leg ached. Eliza put her things away and bustled out of the room, Kara trailing after her and being put to use as her mother raided her healing stores, plying her with an armful of supplies before they made their way to Lena’s room. 

     

                The air was cool as Kara stepped inside, setting everything down on an empty shelf before she went to fetch a lamp from her room, lighting it quickly and moving back into the room. Eliza cast her a fleeting look and asked for water, leaving Kara to go off to fetch some before she returned again. Her mother was murmuring softly to Lena’s restlessly writhing form as she sighed listlessly, her face a flushed furrow. Sweat made her shift cling to her and her hair was like ink across the pillows, strands sticking to her cheeks and brow.

     

                Dipping a cloth into the frigid water, Kara wrung it out and moved over to the bed, carefully swiping it across Lena’s sweating forehead as she looked down at her pinched face with an unreadable brooding look. Slowly bathing her skin in cool water, Kara stayed out of the way as Eliza checked her shoulder wound - it looked clean enough, no signs of infection - and she applied fresh honey and herbs to it, wrapping it loosely in clean linen bandages and then muttering to herself as she rushed out and returned a short while later with a steaming cup of tea, the medicinal smell of herbs hitting Kara’s nose.

     

                “Let it cool first,” Eliza instructed her. “I’ll fetch her something clean to wear; you keep bathing her.”

     

                Nodding, Kara dipped the cloth into the cold water and squeezed it tightly as she gave her wife a once-over, shifting closer as she moved the sheet down, smoothing the cloth over the collarbones, the sides of her neck, the curve of her jaw. Lena’s eyes rolled beneath closed lids and her lips moved soundlessly. The troubled look on her face was familiar to Kara, who had seen her have more than one nightmare, who knew they were usually of drowning, of death. 

     

                Mopping her damp brow, Kara’s throat felt tight in the stifling silence of the room, thoughts of her angry words, if partially undone thanks to Eliza’s insistence, being the last exchanged with Lena making her feel terribly guilty. Before she could get too wrapped up in her thoughts, her mother returned with a clean cotton nightgown and new sheets for the sweat-dampened bedding. 

     

                “I will do it,” Kara insisted as Eliza set the bundle down.

     

                “As you wish. Let me take a look at your leg first,” Eliza replied, gesturing to the seat.

     

                Sitting and pulling her own cotton nightgown up over her bandaged thigh, Kara extended her leg and let her mother quickly unravel the bandages. The stitches Eliza had finished for Lena were neatly done, the edges faintly pink and tenderly warm as her mother gently probed at them. Fussing over it for a few moments, rinsing it out and adding a new salve, Eliza bandaged it back up and made her daughter drain a cup of tea as well for the dull pain.

     

                Leaving her to her vigil, Eliza left, leaving behind the herbs, bandages and water in case it was needed. Climbing to her feet, Kara dragged the damp sheets off Lena and shook out the clean one, tucking the bottom of it beneath the thin mattress on the stone slab and then keeping the rest of it at Lena’s feet. Sighing, she picked up the nightgown next and gave her wife’s sleeping form a grim look.

     

                “You do not make it easy, do you?” she mumbled as she reached out to ruck up the hem of the one her wife was wearing to swap it for the clean one. “No doubt you’ll be unhappy when you wake and find you have been struck by a fever. I know how you hate to feel so helpless. Still, you’re not angry when you’re asleep so at least we will not be at each other’s throats for a while. That would be preferable to worrying about you though. It almost feels like a near-permanent state for me now. I do wonder if all marriages are as such or whether I have been saddled with the singular most stressful wife in the two Courts and the wilds.”

     

                Kara grumbled her way through changing Lena and brushing her hair out of her face, wiping her skin down again and then making her drink the tea, holding her lolling head propped up as Lena coughed and sputtered until she choked it down. She was unresponsive and Kara basked in the freeing opportunity to speak her mind as she tucked her back in and started a small fire to ward off the chill without raising Lena’s core temperature.

     

                Crouching before the fire as she let the small log catch, Kara almost burnt her hand at the sound of Lena’s hoarse rasp behind her, breaking the heavy silence. “Don’t.”

     

                Whirling around, heart pounding, Kara let out a rough breath and dusted off her hands before climbing back to her feet. She was moving towards the stool when Lena spoke again, her voice a small whimper, childishly vulnerable and pleading.

     

                “Ieiu.”

     

                Quiet devastation cut through Kara as her shoulders sagged, and she found herself sitting on the edge of the stone slab of a bed instead of her stool. Reaching out, she tugged the blankets up over Lena’s chest and tenderly smoothed her hair back as her mouth thinned

     

                “Ieiu. Please. Don’t go. Ieiu. Mom.”

     

                “Shh, okhahsh, zhao,” Kara murmured in the fae tongue, urging her to sleep, the endearment rolling off her tongue along with the order without her even consciously realising. If she had, she might have wondered why it didn’t trip her up, choke off her words as the lie got caught in her throat. Instead, it came out easily, honestly. “Okhahsh. All is well.”

     

                Brow creasing with consternation, Lena twitched restlessly, a wispy sigh escaping her, and Kara kept murmuring to her as she stroked her dark hair. There was a gentle ache in her chest as she stayed with Lena, the gloom of the deep rooms of the halls making it feel as if they were shrouded in the darkness of night, the silence weighing as heavily as it did.

     

                Speaking softly to her as Kara told stories of her childhood, of the forest and the rivers, lakes and seas, she tried to ease Lena’s troubled dreams. It was only when she started to hum the melodies of old river songs taught to Kara during days spent fishing on the water, weaving nets and hooking trout for supper, that Lena’s restlessness eased. Kara found herself holding her hand somehow, the smoothness of her palm, save for the little callouses on the fingers she used to draw back her bowstring, an oddity. 

     

                Kara was used to the roughness of hands spent climbing trees, carving wood, hauling ropes and holding sword hilts. Not the gentle softness of hands that had held flowers more than weapons, that cradled books and clumsily held quills, Lena’s erudition more apparent than her affinity for battle. 

     

                Thinking hard about what had transpired and what to do next, Kara idled away most of the morning alone with her thoughts. A flicker of movement caught her attention before noon and she straightened on her seat, blinking owlishly as she looked at her sister and dropped Lena’s hand. 

     

                Her muscles were stiff and she rolled her shoulders as Alex stepped further inside without a word, climbing to her feet to stretch and then sitting back on her stool. Alex stood just inside the gloomy doorway and stared at Lena for a long moment, neither of them speaking as the small fire crackled.

     

                “How is she?”

     

                “She has not woken yet. She is restless though; she never sleeps well. Nightmares. She-” Kara faltered for a moment, her expression softening with sorrow. “She keeps calling for her mother.”

     

                “Shame. For one to have suffered a loss such as that so young.”

     

                “It’s why she and I will never- there is no fondness for me in her heart because of what has been taken from her. It was a terrible crime, what was done to her mother by the Unseelie but … I fear it was a foolish decision for her mother to take her from here. Now … she will never feel safe, never trust anyone here. No matter what I do, I will always be one of the people who took her mother from her, even if she is half of us herself. It makes a difficult time for us both in this marriage.”

     

                “How goes it?”

     

                Sighing heavily, Kara shook her head and felt her frustration well up as words started spilling out of her, stamped down for so long with no one to share them with but the object of their origin. “She is stubbornly opposed to feeling even the slightest bit of fondness for me. My very being seems to offend her, as if my mere existence is an affront to her own. I may have agreed to this but I didn’t want it as much as she didn’t want it, and now I am left as a guard, tutor and companion to a woman who seems to take satisfaction in undermining my every effort to help her. I barely managed to get us both out of the Unseelie Court alive and you know what her response was to her foolishness? That she never asked me to save her.”

     

                “Mistakes are to be expected.”

     

                Huffing, Kara raked a hand through her unbound hair, a river of gold spilling down her back as she hunched forward, brooding as she looked at the starkly pale face of her sleeping wife. “And I expect mistakes, I would not hold them against her or behave harshly towards her for them, only assassination plots are not mistakes. ”

     

                Nodding, Alex leaned against the wall, arms folded over her chest as she stared at Lena as well, her brown eyes darting to Kara every so often as she took in the intensity of her sister’s stare. After a moment, she softly cleared her throat and straightened against the wall, shoulders set as she gave her opinion.

     

                “And what has been done to make her feel safe? Welcome? What friends does she have in this place? Who to trust?”

     

                “I- me. I have tried to befriend her. I have tried giving her compliments. Once I told her she has fingernails like fish scales; you would have thought I’d spat at her feet. Another time I said her hair was like seaweed - you know, the silken kind - and she was so affronted I was left trying to understand what could have insulted her. Another time I said her eyes were the colour of algae in that specific lighting - mind you, I believe her eyes to be a near perfect shade of jade ordinarily but in this instance-“

     

                Alex groaned, tipping her head back before she kneaded her brow and gave her sister an exasperated look. “You are giving her Waterfolk compliments.”

     

                “And what is wrong with that?” Kara indignantly replied.

     

                “When I was courting Kelly-“

     

                “Now that is an entirely different circumstance. She’s my wife and there is no love lost between us .”

     

                “If you are not interested in my advice, I shall go,” Alex snidely said as she straightened and angled towards the door.

     

                “No, wait,” Kara anxiously stopped her, delicate features drawn with stress as she reached out for her sister. “Please.”

     

                Sighing, Alex gestured towards the unconscious princess. “As I said, when I was courting Kelly, I didn’t tell her that she smelled of sweet smoke from burning apple wood, I told her she was like a cool breeze on a hot summer’s day. And you, I would not describe you as stubborn as a raging forest first, I would say you are strong like a river.”

     

                “I- well …” Kara faltered.

     

                Exhaling heavily, Alex crossed over to her and clapped Kara on the shoulder, giving her a weary look. “Just tell her she’s as beautiful as a rose in full bloom. Is it so difficult for you to say that?”

     

                Brow furrowing as she looked over at Lena, Kara’s mouth thinned and she murmured distractedly to herself. “A rose. Yes, flowers will do. She is fond of flowers.”

     

                Looking at Alex with a wary look in her blue eyes, Kara gently bit her lip as she hesitated. “She- she is beautiful, isn’t she?”

     

                A smile fought at the corners of Alex’s mouth and she nodded. “She is. She is just like a rose; beautiful but full of thorns.”

     

                Kara hummed dubiously and smoothed her thumb over her bottom lip as she considered her sister’s words. Softly sighing, Alex gave her shoulder a quick pat and then kissed the top of Kara’s head.
